newsitem.title: UK: RMC shares helped by CRH comments.
newsitem.headline: RMC shares helped by CRH comments.

text.p: Shares in building materials company RMC Group Plc advanced on Tuesday on the back of comments from Irish firm CRH Plc and as sentiment surrounding the sector's European interests improved, traders said.
Shares in RMC Group were up 13p at 972p by 1003 GMT. Since September, the stock has been in a steady decline, losing 24 percent to lows of 905p in January this year.

Annual results from Irish building materials supplier CRH helped to buck the trend. CRH said it expected Britain to start showing signs of a return to growth in 1997 after failing to achieve its promised lift-off in 1996.
The company also commented that the weather over the winter period had been favourable for the construction industry. "We have not had the prolonged freeze-up of 1996," the company said.
Industry analysts said there was also renewed optimism over the prospects of companies with substantial interests in Continental Europe.

"We have seen people raise their stance towards the European capital goods and building stocks," said one head of equity sales. "There have been two "buy" recommendations recently on the German company Dyckerhoff AG," he added.
"RMC is a notoriously unmarketable stock which is now benefiting from these upgrades and beginning to play catch-up," the salesman said.
"Continental Europe has been a negative factor for the stock up until now because these economies have been lagging and the pound has been strengthening."
